questions.question: According to Mead's research, how does child-rearing influence personality development across different cultures? Explain.
questions.solution_html:
• Ruth Benedict emphasized how cultural patterns shape the collective personality of
  • societies, describing culture as a "personality writ large." She studied specific cultures, like
  • the Zuni and Dobu, to highlight their unique traits. Margaret Mead, however, focused on
  • how childhood socialization within different cultures influences personality development.
  • Her work, like the study of adolescence in Samoa, demonstrated the flexibility of human
  • behaviour across cultures. While Benedict emphasized the overarchi ng cultural
  • framework, Mead highlighted the role of individual upbringing and social structures.
